Establishment of Paid  Establishment of Paid Employee Childcare Program - In response to the

Employee Childcare Program  Covid- 19 pandemic as well as federal legislation providing employees
  additional paid leave provisions and needing employees to report to work to
  provide essential services, the City implemented a childcare program on
  March 30, 2020. Staff asked the City Council to consider formalizing the
  program in consideration of the pandemic' s prolonged effect on other available
  childcare services.

  City Manager Russi reported that a request was received from a La Verne
  resident asking that the Childcare Program be extended to La Verne residents.
  He stated that due to licensing problems and the City' s Insurance' s carrier
  would not permit it; it would not be possible to offer to residents.

  Staff recommended that the City Council direct staff to formally develop a
  childcare program for employee dependents and charge $ 30 per day per child
  to participate effective August 3, 2020. Approved.

8.  Agreement for Temporary  City Manager Russi reported on the agreement for temporary employment for
  Employment Interim Fire Chief  Interim Fire Chief. He stated that Interim Fire Chief Devin Leonard has
  David Segura  provided notification he will be leaving his position effective August 12, 2020.
  After conducting a search of qualified replacements, David Segura has been
  selected to serve as Interim Fire Chief while the City conducts recruitment for a
  permanent replacement. In order to be compliant with the 2013 Pension
  Reform Act, it is necessary for the City Council to take an action affirming the
  execution of such employment arrangements. Resolution No. 20- 69 and
  agreement satisfies that requirement.

  Mayor Hepburn called for any public announcements on this matter and waited
  for staff to check for any announcements via telephone communication.

  Jim Murphy, La Verne resident communicated his public comment via
  telephone communication.

  The La Verne City Council thanked Interim Fire Chief Leonard for his service
  and wished him well on his retirement.

  It was moved by Carder, seconded by Davis, and unanimously carried to
  approve Resolution No. 20- 69, authorizing the City Manager to execute an
  agreement with David Segura to provide temporary, part-time employment.

9.  Continued to August 17, 2020  At the request of the applicant, the Appeal Hearing was continued to the
  August 17, 2020 Council Meeting.

  Appeal  Hearing -  1820 Walnut  Appeal Hearing -  1820 Walnut Street- Illegal Construction - The Building
  Street - Illegal Construction  Department has issued a Stop Work Notice and a Notice of Substandard for
  the property at 1820 Walnut Street as there was a report of illegal construction
  of a new single- family residence on the property in April 2020. The property
  owners, Richard T. Landi and Shellie M. Hartwick, have subsequently, through
  their attorney Thomas A. Nitti, filed a claim against the City and have appealed
  the two notices as allowed for by the Los Angeles County Code, which the
  City' s Municipal Code adopts by reference. The City Council, sitting as the
  Building Rehabilitation Appeals Board, should hear the appeal and determine if
  the two notices should be rescinded.

10.  Public Comment  This was the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on
  items not listed in any other place on the agenda. Mayor Hepburn called for
  public comment and waited for staff to check for any public comment via
  telephone communication.

  La Verne resident Richard Bowen commented via phone communication.

  Two public comments received via email ( attached).

11.  Council Comments  Mayor Pro Tem Carder stated she fully supported City Manager Russi. She
  stated that he is doing a great job especially his leadership during the COVID-
  19 pandemic in protecting the community and employees.

  Council Member Crosby thanked Interim Fire Chief Leonard for his service.
  He stated that the outdoor restaurant dining in downtown is a success and that
  staff did a great job in making it happen.

  Council Member Lau welcomed new Interim Fire Chief David Segura. She
  reported on a forum hosted by ULV College of Law and the La Verne Chamber
  of Commerce on the Impacts of COVID- 19 on businesses. She urged
  residents to support local businesses and Eat La Verne.

  Council Member Davis reported on the La Verne/ San Dimas Educational
  Foundation and on the Public Bank Pomona Valley meetings.

  Mayor Hepburn also welcomed new Interim Fire Chief Segura. He stated he
  agreed with Mayor Pro Tern Carder's statement that City Manager Russi is
  doing a great job in responding to the COVID- 19 pandemic and so was staff.
  He thanked the Community Development staff for their prompt response and
  assistance in helping local businesses and residents. He stated that Eat La
  Verne is doing well and the businesses were doing well. He urged residents to
  wear their mask, practice social distancing, wash hands and reach out to
  family and friends.

13.  Adjournment at 9: 06 pm, in memory of Charles E. Davis, long- time La Verne resident who passed away on July
  1, 2020. He was born in La Verne, California. He graduated from Bonita High School and attended La Verne
  College. Charles was a printer, a conscientious objector, a professor of graphic arts management, business
  owner, and an adult schoolteacher. He is survived by his wife Mildred of 74 years and his children, Alan
  Margaret) Kathryn ( Carl), and Robbie ( Libby).  Council Member Davis also spoke fondly of his Uncle Charles
  La Verne,
  with a  story of how he helped in the printing
  and  binding of the book on the history of La Verne, titled "
  The Story of the People who Made a Difference" (A history of La Verne 1837- 1987) written by La Verne Historian
  Evelyn Hollinger.

  and

  In memory of Elizabeth ( Liz) Marie Hernandez, long-time La Verne resident who passed away on July 14, 2020.
  Liz spent her childhood in Duarte, California, and her family moved to the City of La Verne in 1973. She
  graduated from Bonita High School. After High School, she worked for a pharmaceutical company and later was
  employed by the United States Post Office as a mail carrier for 20- plus years. Liz had a huge caring heart, she
  was good a friend to all, and she loved her family. Liz is survived by her sister Trish ( Patty), brother Ralph, three
  nephews, four nieces, and thirteen great nieces and nephews.
